data.text: [00:00]CD2 Track 10
G = Georgia, J = Jenny, I = Ivan, M = Madison
[00:05.5]Hello?
[00:14]Oh, Georgia … this is Jenny … I’m so sorry. `[00:18]Did I wake you up?
[00:19]Ermm … no, well … not really …
[00:23.9]Oh dear … you sound terrible. `[00:27]How are you?
[00:28.8]Not very well, really. `[00:31]I’ve got an awful sore throat and I can’t stop coughing …
[00:34.6]Poor you! `[00:36]Have you taken anything for it?
[00:39]Ermm … well, no …

[00:42.1]I remember having a sore throat a lot when I was a child … and my mother always gave me hot water with honey and lemon. `[00:49.9]Why don’t you try drinking some of that? `[00:52]It really helps.
[00:54]Thanks. `[00:55]That’s a good idea.
[00:57]Have you got any honey or lemon at home?
[01:00]Erm … well … I don’t think I’ve got any honey, no.
[01:05.8]Well, listen – on the way to college, I’ll stop to get some honey at the supermarket and bring it round.
[01:13]Oh, no … don’t worry about that …
[01:16.9]… It’s not a problem – don’t worry … . `[01:19.5]And try not to cough too much … . `[01:22]You should go back to bed now …
[01:25]Yes, I think I’ll do that …
[01:28]I’ll come round in about half an hour.
[01:31]OK … thanks, Jenny. `[01:34]Oh … will you remember to get the homework for me?
[01:38.3]That’s fine … . `[01:39.5]See you later.
[01:41]Bye.
[01:56]Hello?
[01:57]Hello? `[01:59]Georgia, is that you?
[02:01]Yes …
[02:06]Oh dear … I hope I didn’t wake you up. `[02:10]It’s Ivan here. I got your email and I wanted to check you were OK … . `[02:17]Do you need anything?
[02:19]It’s really kind of you to phone, Ivan … . `[02:22]Erm, I think I just need to sleep really … and Jenny is going to bring me some honey and lemon for my sore throat.
[02:32]Honey and lemon? `[02:34]Oh really, that’s an English remedy, isn’t it?
[02:38]Yes … I suppose it is.
[02:41]Well, have you tried having honey and butter in hot milk? `[02:46]In Russia, my grandmother always gave us that. `[02:50]I remember having it a lot when I was a child.
[02:53]Erm, … I haven’t tried that. `[02:56.5]Did you say it’s a Russian remedy?
[03:00]Yes … it’s really good. `[03:03]I used to love it and it makes your throat feel much better. `[03:07]Would you like me to come and see you? `[03:10]I could bring some round for you to try.
[03:12.8]Oh, no … really. `[03:15]It’s fine … I mean, Jenny will be here soon.
[03:21]It’s no bother really. `[03:23]I’ll just come in on my way to college. `[03:26]Try to get some sleep now.
[03:29]Ermm … OK – see you in about half an hour …
[03:38]Hello?
[03:46.4]Georgia? `[03:48]Hi, it’s Madison here.
[03:50]Oh, hi …
[03:51.8]You don’t sound very well. `[03:53.5]How are you?
[03:55.5]I’m not feeling very well …
[03:57.9]Were you asleep? `[03:59]Sorry – I probably woke you up, didn’t I?
[04:03]Well … it’s really nice of everyone to phone me. `[04:06]I mean, Jenny and Ivan just phoned and … well, it’s lovely really …
[04:13.6]But you can’t sleep …
[04:16]Well, yes … I suppose …
[04:22.8]Oh dear … you have got a bad cough. `[04:25.5]You should have honey and vinegar in hot water.
[04:30]Honey and vinegar?! `[04:31]Oh, I don’t fancy that!

[04:34.7]It’s good! `[04:35]You use apple vinegar. `[04:37.8]It’s an old American remedy. `[04:39.9]My mom used to give it to us children when we were ill. `[04:43.3]It smells bad, but it’s really delicious and … it makes your throat feel better.
[04:49]Really? `[04:51]Jenny said the English remedy is hot water with honey and lemon. `[04:56]Ivan said the Russian remedy is hot milk with honey and butter, and …

[05:03]Oh! I’m so sorry. `[05:04]You’ve got all the advice you need, haven’t you? `[05:07]Well, OK … I know what you really need – you need some rest … and some peace and quiet. `[05:14.8]You need people to stop phoning you! `[05:17.9]Why don’t you try turning your phone off?
[05:20]Yes, that’s a good idea. `[05:23]Oh! That’s Jenny, I think … with the honey and lemon … or it could be Ivan. `[05:32]Sorry Madison, I’d better go and answer the door.
[05:36.8]OK … look after yourself – and try to get some rest.
[05:41.7]Bye.
